# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Exact inclusion-minimal clause discovery for the finite window protocol.
#
# A clause is a nonempty set of predicate ids and means their disjunction.  A
# clause covers a window when at least one of its literals is true on it, so
# the clauses that satisfy every training window are exactly the hitting sets
# of the per-window true-literal evidence sets.  Condition 2 of the protocol is
# inclusion minimality of those hitting sets, which lets the search stop at the
# first covering prefix of every branch: any strict superset of a covering set
# is still covering and therefore never minimal.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def _lowest_set_bit(value: int) -> int:
    """Index of the lowest set bit of a positive Python int."""
    return (value & -value).bit_length() - 1


def enumerate_minimal_clauses(
    literal_train_masks: list[int],
    literal_universe_masks: list[int],
    max_clause_size: int,
) -> list[tuple[tuple[int, ...], int]]:
    """Return every inclusion-minimal clause of length <= ``max_clause_size``.

    ``literal_train_masks[i]`` has bit ``r`` set when literal ``i`` is true on
    training window ``r``; ``literal_universe_masks[i]`` has bit ``u`` set when
    literal ``i`` is true on universe window ``u``.  The result holds each
    clause together with its universe truth mask so callers can derive
    counterexamples without recomputation.  Clauses are returned in discovery
    order; ordering by ``(length, ids)`` is the caller's concern.
    """
    literal_count = len(literal_train_masks)
    train_count = max((mask.bit_length() for mask in literal_train_masks), default=0)
    full_train = (1 << train_count) - 1
    universe_count = max((mask.bit_length() for mask in literal_universe_masks), default=0)
    full_universe = (1 << universe_count) - 1
    train_masks = literal_train_masks
    universe_masks = literal_universe_masks
    found: list[tuple[tuple[int, ...], int]] = []

    def extend(chosen: tuple[int, ...], covered: int, start: int) -> None:
        for candidate in range(start, literal_count):
            mask = train_masks[candidate]
            fresh = mask & ~covered
            if not fresh:
                # The candidate adds no coverage, so it would be a redundant
                # literal of any covering extension: skip the whole branch.
                continue
            next_covered = covered | fresh
            if next_covered == full_train:
                clause = chosen + (candidate,)
                for literal in clause:
                    if (next_covered & ~train_masks[literal]) == full_train:
                        break
                else:
                    truth = 0
                    for literal in clause:
                        truth |= universe_masks[literal]
                    if truth != full_universe:
                        found.append((clause, truth))
                continue
            if len(chosen) + 1 < max_clause_size:
                extend(chosen + (candidate,), next_covered, candidate + 1)

    if train_count:
        extend((), 0, 0)
    return found
